title: VI–X. Law defined; law of nature and human law
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): it not only orders ye human's actions but also forbids actions by which occasion belonging toward sinning stands as given toward others. — Ye law belonging toward God requires perfect obedience with all powers; — Ye divine law in itself stands as nothing other than ye idea belonging toward ye divine will concerning things toward be done and omitted. — Distinctions stand as toward be observed here. — VI. — Ye law belonging toward nature as it now stands as in humans after ye fall still retains certain sparks by which sin stands as rebuked. — Ye law belonging toward NATURE stands as ye light and dictate belonging toward right reason by which a human naturally discerns ye honorable from ye base. — VIII. — Law stands as either belonging toward nature, or human, or divine. — VII. — Human law stands as a definite sentence belonging toward right issued by ye magistrate toward governing civil society. — X.
pass_b_english: VI. Distinctions are to be observed here. The divine law in itself is nothing other than the idea of the divine will concerning things to be done and omitted. The law of God requires perfect obedience with all powers; it not only orders the human's actions but also forbids actions by which occasion of sinning is given to others.

VII. Law is either of nature, or human, or divine. VIII. The law of NATURE is the light and dictate of right reason by which a human naturally discerns the honorable from the base. The law of nature as it now is in humans after the fall still retains certain sparks by which sin is rebuked.
X. Human law is a definite sentence of right issued by the magistrate for governing civil society.
source_text: VI. Sunt autem hic observandi distinctiones. Lex divina in se nihil aliud est quam idea voluntatis divinae de rebus agendis & omittendis. Lex Dei requirit obedientiam perfectam omnibusque viribus; non tantum ordinat actiones hominis, verum etiam vetat actiones quibus aliis peccandi occasio datur. VII. Est autem lex vel naturae, vel humana, vel divina. VIII. Lex NATURAE est lumen & dictamen rectae rationis, quo homo naturaliter discernit honestum a turpi. Lex naturae, qualis jam est in hominibus post lapsum, scintillas quasdam adhuc retinet quibus peccatum redarguitur. X. Lex humana est definita iuris sententia a magistratu lata ad regendam societatem civilem.
